findings.title: Device limit is bypassed after the first request
findings.body: tagDeviceUI writes the device cache key before CreateOrUpdateDevice returns. When the store is at the limit, a new device's first TagDevice call fails with ErrDeviceLimitReached (so Authenticate denies that request), but the key is already cached for 29 minutes. Every later request for that device ID hits the cache and returns nil without touching the database, so anonymous authentication succeeds and the device is never counted. The configured limit therefore only fails a single attempt per device per cache TTL and does not actually cap anonymous access.

findings.title: Device limit check is not atomic with the insert
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice reads CountDevices and, only if the count is still under deviceLimit, performs a separate INSERT. Those steps are not in one transaction and are not serialized with the existing server lock, so concurrent anonymous requests (including across Grafana replicas sharing the database) can all observe count < limit and all insert. The configured cap can be exceeded by the number of in-flight creates, and nothing in the schema enforces the limit.

findings.title: New auth.anonymous device_limit setting is undocumented
findings.body: AnonymousDeviceLimit is read from auth.anonymous device_limit (default 0, meaning unlimited), but this change does not add the key to defaults.ini / sample.ini or any docs. Operators have no documented way to discover the setting, its default, or that 0 disables enforcement, so the feature cannot be configured as intended.
